```{r setup}
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(mgcv)
# m.formula_joint, process_data(), and the effect extractors used for the main results
source(here("R", "analysis-model.R"))
cache_dir <- here("output", "sensitivity", "trend-spec")
```

```{r covariates}
# Observed weekly counts by outcome. download_obs() set weeks with negative
# counts to NA; carry the last observed week forward so every specification
# fits the same forecasts.
obs <- c(Cases = "case", Deaths = "death") |>
  map(\(x) read_csv(here("data", paste0("observed-", x, ".csv")),
                    show_col_types = FALSE)) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "Epi_target") |>
  arrange(Epi_target, location, target_end_date) |>
  group_by(Epi_target, location) |>
  mutate(
    carried = is.na(observed),
    observed = zoo::na.locf(observed, na.rm = FALSE),
    # Trend as in download_obs(): ratio of 3-week moving averages one week
    # apart, cut at ±5%
    ma = zoo::rollmean(observed, k = 3, align = "right", fill = NA),
    ratio = ma / lag(ma),
    Trend_new = ifelse(is.nan(ratio), "Stable",
                       ifelse(ratio >= 1.05, "Increasing",
                              ifelse(ratio <= 0.95, "Decreasing", "Stable"))),
    Incidence = log(observed + 1),
    # any carried-forward week among the four read by trend and growth
    carried_window = zoo::rollapply(carried, 4, any, align = "right",
                                    fill = NA)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Recomputed trend matches download_obs() wherever no week was carried forward
stopifnot(with(filter(obs, !is.na(trend), !carried_window),
               all(Trend_new == trend)))

# Growth: average weekly change in log incidence over the past 3 weeks
obs <- obs |>
  left_join(
    transmute(obs, Epi_target, location,
              target_end_date = target_end_date + weeks(3),
              Incidence_lag3 = Incidence),
    by = c("Epi_target", "location", "target_end_date")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    ungroup(classify_variant_phases()),
    by = c("location", "target_end_date")
  ) |>
  transmute(Epi_target, location, week = target_end_date, Incidence,
            Trend = Trend_new, VariantPhase,
            growth = (Incidence - Incidence_lag3) / 3, carried_window)

# Join covariates to each forecast at the target week and at the forecast date
# (the last complete week before the forecast: target week minus horizon)
at_week <- function(d, week_col, suffix) {
  cov <- rename_with(obs, \(x) paste0(x, suffix),
                     -c(Epi_target, location, week))
  left_join(d, cov, by = c("Epi_target", Location = "location",
                           setNames("week", week_col)))
}
scores <- process_data("log") |>
  filter(!grepl("EuroCOVIDhub-ensemble", Model), !is.na(wis)) |>
  select(-any_of(c("Incidence", "Trend", "VariantPhase"))) |>
  mutate(Epi_target = epi_target,
         forecast_week = target_end_date - weeks(Horizon))
trend_levels <- c("Stable", "Increasing", "Decreasing")
covariates <- scores |>
  at_week("target_end_date", "_target") |>
  at_week("forecast_week", "_forecast") |>
  mutate(
    growth_realised = (Incidence_target - Incidence_forecast) / Horizon,
    Epi_target = factor(Epi_target),
    Location = factor(Location),
    across(starts_with("Trend_"), \(x) factor(x, levels = trend_levels)),
    across(starts_with("VariantPhase_"), factor)
  )
n_scored <- nrow(covariates)
covariates <- covariates |>
  filter(if_all(c(Incidence_target, Trend_target, VariantPhase_target,
                  Incidence_forecast, Trend_forecast, VariantPhase_forecast,
                  growth_forecast), \(x) !is.na(x)))
```

```{r specifications}
# Each step changes one thing from the previous one. Step 0 is the primary
# model as specified in R/analysis-model.R.
specs <- tribble(
  ~step, ~label, ~previous, ~dates, ~growth, ~terms, ~change,
  "0", "current", NA, "target", NA,
  's(Incidence) + s(Trend, bs = "re")',
  "Current primary model",
  "1", "forecast-date", "current", "forecast", NA,
  's(Incidence) + s(Trend, bs = "re")',
  "Covariates at the forecast date",
  "2", "incidence-by", "forecast-date", "forecast", NA,
  's(Incidence, by = Epi_target) + s(Trend, bs = "re")',
  "Incidence by outcome",
  "3", "growth", "incidence-by", "forecast", "forecast",
  "s(Incidence, by = Epi_target) + s(growth)",
  "Trend replaced by growth",
  "4", "growth-by", "growth", "forecast", "forecast",
  "s(Incidence, by = Epi_target) + s(growth, by = Epi_target)",
  "Growth by outcome",
  "5", "growth-incidence", "growth-by", "forecast", "forecast",
  paste("s(Incidence, by = Epi_target) + s(growth, by = Epi_target)",
        '+ ti(Incidence, growth, by = Epi_target, bs = c("ts", "ts"))'),
  "Growth by incidence interaction",
  "R", "realised-growth", "growth", "forecast", "realised",
  "s(Incidence, by = Epi_target) + s(growth)",
  "Step 3 with growth from the forecast date to the target week"
)

base_formula <- update(m.formula_joint,
                       . ~ . - s(Incidence) - s(Trend, bs = "re"))
spec_formula <- function(terms) {
  update(base_formula, as.formula(paste(". ~ . +", terms)))
}
spec_data <- function(dates, growth) {
  covariates |>
    mutate(
      Incidence = .data[[paste0("Incidence_", dates)]],
      Trend = .data[[paste0("Trend_", dates)]],
      VariantPhase = .data[[paste0("VariantPhase_", dates)]],
      growth = if (is.na(growth)) NA_real_ else .data[[paste0("growth_", growth)]]
    )
}
# Step 0 has the same terms as the primary model (order aside)
term_labels <- \(f) attr(terms(f), "term.labels")
stopifnot(setequal(term_labels(spec_formula(specs$terms[1])),
                   term_labels(m.formula_joint)))
```

```{r fits}
# Fit one specification and keep a small summary; reuse the cache when the
# formula and number of forecasts match
fit_spec <- function(spec) {
  f <- spec_formula(spec$terms)
  d <- spec_data(spec$dates, spec$growth)
  path <- file.path(cache_dir, paste0(spec$label, ".rds"))
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    out <- readRDS(path)
    if (identical(out$formula, deparse1(f)) && out$n == nrow(d)) return(out)
    message("cache stale, refitting: ", spec$label)
  }
  message("-------- fitting: ", spec$label)
  time <- system.time(
    fit <- bam(f, data = d, family = tw(link = "log"),
               method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE)
  )[["elapsed"]]
  smooth_labels <- keep(map_chr(fit$smooth, "label"),
                        \(x) grepl("Incidence|growth", x))
  out <- list(
    label = spec$label,
    formula = deparse1(f),
    n = nrow(d),
    time_s = time,
    edf = sum(fit$edf),
    dev_expl = summary(fit)$dev.expl,
    aic = AIC(fit),
    tweedie_p = fit$family$getTheta(TRUE),
    converged = fit$converged,
    s_table = as_tibble(summary(fit)$s.table, rownames = "term"),
    method = method_pooled_effects(fit),
    method_by_target = method_target_effects(fit),
    model = model_horizon_effects(fit),
    ranef = extract_ranef_terms(fit),
    smooths = bind_rows(
      gratia::smooth_estimates(fit, n = 200,
                               select = discard(smooth_labels, \(x) grepl("^ti", x))),
      if (any(grepl("^ti", smooth_labels)))
        gratia::smooth_estimates(fit, n = 60,
                                 select = keep(smooth_labels, \(x) grepl("^ti", x)))
    ),
    concurvity = tryCatch(concurvity(fit, full = TRUE),
                          error = \(e) conditionMessage(e))
  )
  dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(out, path)
  rm(fit)
  gc()
  out
}
fits <- specs |>
  split(seq_len(nrow(specs))) |>
  map(fit_spec) |>
  set_names(specs$label)
```

## Summary

<!-- P0 purpose: what changed, step by step; each step changes one thing from the previous one -->

<!-- S2 recommended primary specification: step ___ -->

```{r summary-table}
compare_fits <- function(a, b) {
  m <- inner_join(a$method, b$method, by = "group", suffix = c("", "_ref"))
  r <- inner_join(a$model, b$model, by = "group", suffix = c("", "_ref"))
  tibble(aic_change = a$aic - b$aic,
         method_shift = max(abs(m$value - m$value_ref)),
         rank_cor = cor(r$value, r$value_ref, method = "spearman"))
}
specs |>
  mutate(
    dev_expl = map_dbl(label, \(l) 100 * fits[[l]]$dev_expl),
    vs_previous = map2(label, previous, \(l, p) {
      if (is.na(p)) tibble(aic_change = NA, method_shift = NA, rank_cor = NA)
      else compare_fits(fits[[l]], fits[[p]])
    }),
    vs_current = map(label, \(l) compare_fits(fits[[l]], fits[["current"]]))
  ) |>
  unnest_wider(vs_previous) |>
  unnest_wider(vs_current, names_sep = "_") |>
  select(Step = step, Change = change,
         `Deviance explained (%)` = dev_expl,
         `AIC change` = aic_change,
         `Max structure shift` = method_shift,
         `Rank correlation` = rank_cor,
         `Max structure shift vs current` = vs_current_method_shift,
         `Rank correlation vs current` = vs_current_rank_cor) |>
  kable(digits = c(0, 0, 1, 0, 3, 2, 3, 2),
        caption = "Each step compared with the previous step (step R with step 3) and with the current model. Structure shift: largest change in a pooled model structure effect, log scale. Rank correlation: Spearman correlation of individual model effects.")
```

```{r summary-structure}
#| fig-cap: "Pooled model structure effects at each step, as ratios of expected LWIS with 95% intervals."
#| fig-height: 5
fits[specs$label[specs$step != "R"]] |>
  map(\(f) f$method) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "label") |>
  left_join(select(specs, label, step, change), by = "label") |>
  mutate(step = paste(step, change, sep = ": "),
         step = factor(step, rev(unique(step)))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = exp(value), y = group, colour = step)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = exp(lower_2.5), xmax = exp(upper_97.5)),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), size = 0.2) +
  scale_colour_grey(start = 0.8, end = 0, guide = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  labs(x = "Ratio of expected LWIS", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Forecaster's dilemma

### The dilemma

This is a problem where we adjust for incidence, trend and variant phase.
In the first version of this work, we modelled these outcome-linked covariates at the target week, thereby conditioning on the outcome.

<!-- S2 consequence: forecaster's dilemma (Lerch et al. 2017): ___ -->

After some discussion (#187), we decided to do things properly and include covariates at the forecast date. 
At the same time, there is still a meaningful interpretation of values by target date. It helps to adjust for performance as realised difficulty, versus predictable difficulty.

| Question | Covariate timing | Use here |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Does model structure matter? | either; forecast date is stricter | forecast date primary; target week as robustness |
| Why does performance vary across targets? | forecast date: foreseeable difficulty; target week: realised difficulty | forecast date primary; target week in supplement |
| Which model to trust? | forecast date only | forecast date |

### Variables affected

<!-- P2 purpose: which covariates move, and by how much -->

<!-- S1 incidence, trend and variant phase all join on target_end_date (R/process-data.R) -->

<!-- S2 evidence: agreement between the two dates falls with horizon for all three (table) -->

<!-- S3 variant phase: handled by the date change only -->

<!-- S4 weeks with negative counts carried forward from the last observed week: ___ forecasts (table, last column) -->

```{r covariate-agreement}
covariates |>
  group_by(Outcome = Epi_target, Horizon) |>
  summarise(
    Forecasts = n(),
    `Trend agrees (%)` = 100 * mean(Trend_target == Trend_forecast),
    `Variant phase agrees (%)` =
      100 * mean(VariantPhase_target == VariantPhase_forecast),
    `Log incidence correlation` = cor(Incidence_target, Incidence_forecast),
    `Carried-forward week` = sum(carried_window_forecast, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  kable(digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0),
        caption = paste0("Agreement between each covariate at the forecast date and in the target week. Carried-forward week: forecasts whose forecast-date covariates read a week with negative counts. ",
                         n_scored - nrow(covariates), " of ", n_scored,
                         " scored forecasts excluded for a missing covariate."))
```

## Handling incidence

### Current

<!-- P3 S1: log(Incidence + 1) of raw weekly counts in the target week; one s(Incidence) shared by cases and deaths (R/analysis-model.R) -->

### Forecast date

<!-- P4 S1: same term, incidence in the last complete week before the forecast date -->

<!-- S2 evidence: log incidence correlation between dates (table above) -->

### As an epidemic process

<!-- P5 purpose: log scale -->

<!-- S1 claim: incidence is logged to mirror the log-transformed scores; already in the current model; the natural-scale fit keeps counts -->

<!-- S2 ___ -->

<!-- P6 purpose: by outcome -->

<!-- S1 problem: a shared curve gives deaths the cases shape, shifted by a constant -->

<!-- S2 problem: death counts are 172-fold below case counts (median across 32 countries of each country's median weekly cases over median weekly deaths, weeks ending 7 March 2021 to 10 March 2023), so the outcomes barely overlap (rug); the low end of the curve competes with the Epi_target intercept -->

<!-- S3 fix: s(Incidence, by = Epi_target) -->

<!-- S4 effect on estimates: ___ (figure, step 2) -->

```{r incidence-effects}
#| fig-cap: "Incidence effect at steps 0 to 2, as ratios of expected LWIS with 95% intervals. Steps 0 and 1 share one curve across outcomes. Ticks: incidence of a sample of forecasts by outcome, at the forecast date."
#| fig-height: 4
inc_rug <- covariates |>
  slice_sample(n = 2000) |>
  transmute(Outcome = Epi_target, Incidence = Incidence_forecast)
# Smooths by outcome are evaluated over the pooled range; show each outcome
# only over its own observed range
observed_range <- covariates |>
  group_by(Outcome = as.character(Epi_target)) |>
  summarise(inc_min = min(Incidence_forecast), inc_max = max(Incidence_forecast),
            .groups = "drop")
fits[c("current", "forecast-date", "incidence-by")] |>
  map(\(f) filter(f$smooths, grepl("Incidence", .smooth))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "label") |>
  left_join(select(specs, label, step, change), by = "label") |>
  mutate(panel = factor(paste(step, change, sep = ": ")),
         Outcome = coalesce(as.character(Epi_target), "Shared")) |>
  left_join(observed_range, by = "Outcome") |>
  filter(Outcome == "Shared" | between(Incidence, inc_min, inc_max)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Incidence, y = exp(.estimate))) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = exp(.estimate - 1.96 * .se),
                  ymax = exp(.estimate + 1.96 * .se), fill = Outcome),
              alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = Outcome)) +
  geom_rug(data = inc_rug, aes(x = Incidence, colour = Outcome),
           inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.2, sides = "b") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, labeller = label_wrap_gen(30)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Cases = "grey20", Deaths = "firebrick",
                                 Shared = "grey50")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Cases = "grey20", Deaths = "firebrick",
                               Shared = "grey50")) +
  labs(x = "Log incidence, log(count + 1)", y = "Ratio of expected LWIS") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Handling trend

### Current

<!-- P7 S1: ratio of 3-week moving averages one week apart, cut at ±5% into increasing, stable, decreasing (R/utils-data.R); measured in the target week -->

<!-- S2 fact: under steady growth the ratio equals exp(weekly growth) of the 3-week moving average of counts, so "stable" is weekly log growth from log(0.95) = -0.051 to log(1.05) = 0.049 -->

<!-- S3 role (Kath, old table): reference: realised difficulty -->

### Forecast date

<!-- P8 S1 evidence: trend at the forecast date matches the target-week trend less often at longer horizons (table above; heatmap) -->

<!-- S2 link: the further ahead the target, the more its trend describes what happened rather than what was knowable -->

<!-- S3 effect on estimates: ___ (trend effects table) -->

<!-- S4 limit (Kath, old table): fixes forecaster's dilemma but is still a weak identification of trend (±5% is arbitrary and doesn't work well across the epicurve) -->

```{r trend-transition}
#| fig-cap: "Trend at the forecast date (rows) against trend in the target week (columns), by outcome and horizon. Each row sums to 100%."
#| fig-height: 5
covariates |>
  count(Epi_target, Horizon, Trend_forecast, Trend_target) |>
  group_by(Epi_target, Horizon, Trend_forecast) |>
  mutate(p = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Trend_target, y = Trend_forecast, fill = p)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(p, accuracy = 1)), size = 2.8) +
  facet_grid(Epi_target ~ Horizon, labeller = labeller(Horizon = label_both)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "firebrick", guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Trend in target week", y = "Trend at forecast date") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
```

```{r trend-effects}
fits[c("current", "forecast-date", "incidence-by")] |>
  map(\(f) filter(f$ranef, group_var == "Trend")) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "label") |>
  left_join(select(specs, label, step), by = "label") |>
  transmute(Trend = group, Step = paste("Step", step),
            ratio = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", exp(value),
                            exp(lower_2.5), exp(upper_97.5))) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Step, values_from = ratio) |>
  kable(caption = "Trend effects as ratios of expected LWIS (95% interval). Step 0: target week; steps 1 and 2: forecast date.")
```

### As an epidemic process

<!-- P9 purpose: define growth -->

<!-- S1 definition: average weekly change in log incidence over the past 3 weeks, ending in the last complete week before the forecast date (sbfnk, #187) -->

<!-- S2 notation, after the words: growth = (log(y_t + 1) - log(y_{t-3} + 1)) / 3 -->

<!-- S3 rationale (Kath, old table): categories to continuous -->

<!-- S4 why 3 weeks: spans the same four weeks as the current trend (weeks -3 to 0), though growth reads only the first and last of them and the trend averages all four (schematic); chosen by principle, not fit -->

<!-- S5 data: finalised counts, not those forecasters saw at the time -->

```{r growth-schematic}
#| fig-cap: "Weeks of data read by each trend or growth measure, for a forecast at horizon 2. Week 0 is the last complete week before the forecast date; the red line marks the forecast date. Schematic."
#| fig-height: 2.5
schematic <- tribble(
  ~measure, ~weeks,
  "Trend, target week (current)", -1:2,
  "Trend, forecast date", -3:0,
  "Growth, forecast date", c(-3, 0),
  "Realised growth", c(0, 2)
) |>
  unnest_longer(weeks) |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, rev(unique(measure))))
ggplot(schematic, aes(x = weeks, y = measure)) +
  geom_tile(data = expand_grid(weeks = -3:2, measure = levels(schematic$measure)),
            fill = "grey95", colour = "white") +
  geom_tile(fill = "grey30", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = -3:2,
                     labels = c("-3", "-2", "-1", "0", "1", "2\ntarget")) +
  labs(x = "Week", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

<!-- P10 purpose: by outcome -->

<!-- S1 claim: growth is scale-free, so both outcomes span the same range; pooling is a choice about effect modification, not a confounded estimate -->

<!-- S2 fit: s(growth, by = Epi_target) -->

<!-- S3 effect on estimates: ___ (figure, steps 3 and 4) -->

<!-- P11 purpose: realised growth, an extended demonstration of why the forecaster's dilemma matters compared to what we have now (Kath, old table) -->

<!-- S1 fit: step 3 with growth from the forecast date to the target week in place of growth before it; diagnostic only, never a candidate -->

<!-- S2 evidence: deviance explained ___ vs ___ for step 3 (summary table, step R) -->

<!-- S3 link: the difference is variation "explained" by information no forecaster had -->

```{r growth-effects}
#| fig-cap: "Growth effect at steps 3 and 4, and for realised growth (step R), as ratios of expected LWIS with 95% intervals. Shown over the central 98% of observed growth."
#| fig-height: 4
growth_range <- quantile(c(covariates$growth_forecast, covariates$growth_realised),
                         c(0.01, 0.99))
fits[c("growth", "growth-by", "realised-growth")] |>
  map(\(f) filter(f$smooths, grepl("^s\\(growth", .smooth))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "label") |>
  left_join(select(specs, label, step, change), by = "label") |>
  mutate(panel = factor(paste(step, change, sep = ": "),
                        unique(paste(step, change, sep = ": "))),
         Outcome = coalesce(as.character(Epi_target), "Shared")) |>
  filter(between(growth, growth_range[1], growth_range[2])) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = growth, y = exp(.estimate))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = exp(.estimate - 1.96 * .se),
                  ymax = exp(.estimate + 1.96 * .se), fill = Outcome),
              alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = Outcome)) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, labeller = label_wrap_gen(30)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Cases = "grey20", Deaths = "firebrick",
                                 Shared = "grey50")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Cases = "grey20", Deaths = "firebrick",
                               Shared = "grey50")) +
  labs(x = "Weekly growth in log incidence", y = "Ratio of expected LWIS") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Additions and interactions

### Current

<!-- P12 S1: additive; no interaction between incidence and trend -->

### Growth and incidence

<!-- P13 S1 question (Kath, old table): whether growth matters differently at high and low incidence -->

<!-- S2 term: ti(Incidence, growth, by = Epi_target, bs = c("ts", "ts")); shrinkage margins let the interaction shrink to near zero, so one fit shows whether it is needed -->

<!-- S3 positivity: surface shown only where at least 10 forecasts fall in a cell -->

<!-- S4 effect on estimates: ___ (table, figure) -->

```{r interaction-table}
conc <- fits[["growth-incidence"]]$concurvity
conc <- if (is.matrix(conc)) {
  tibble(term = colnames(conc), concurvity = conc["estimate", ])
} else {
  tibble(term = character(), concurvity = numeric())
}
fits[["growth-incidence"]]$s_table |>
  filter(grepl("Incidence|growth", term)) |>
  left_join(conc, by = "term") |>
  select(Term = term, edf, `p-value`, Concurvity = concurvity) |>
  kable(digits = c(0, 2, 3, 2),
        caption = "Incidence and growth terms at step 5. An interaction term with edf near zero has been shrunk out. Concurvity: how far each term can be approximated by the rest of the model (0 none, 1 entirely).")
```

```{r interaction-surface}
#| fig-cap: "Interaction between incidence and growth at step 5, on the log scale (0: no interaction), by outcome. Shown over the central 98% of observed growth; cells with fewer than 10 forecasts are blank; colours capped at ±1."
#| fig-height: 4
surface <- fits[["growth-incidence"]]$smooths |>
  filter(grepl("^ti", .smooth))
support <- covariates |>
  transmute(Epi_target, Incidence = Incidence_forecast, growth = growth_forecast)
surface |>
  group_by(Epi_target) |>
  group_modify(\(s, key) {
    d <- filter(support, Epi_target == key$Epi_target)
    breaks_i <- seq(min(s$Incidence), max(s$Incidence), length.out = 31)
    breaks_g <- seq(min(s$growth), max(s$growth), length.out = 31)
    cells <- count(tibble(i = findInterval(d$Incidence, breaks_i, all.inside = TRUE),
                          g = findInterval(d$growth, breaks_g, all.inside = TRUE)),
                   i, g)
    s |>
      mutate(i = findInterval(Incidence, breaks_i, all.inside = TRUE),
             g = findInterval(growth, breaks_g, all.inside = TRUE)) |>
      left_join(cells, by = c("i", "g"))
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(coalesce(n, 0L) >= 10,
         between(growth, growth_range[1], growth_range[2])) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Incidence, y = growth, fill = .estimate)) +
  geom_raster() +
  facet_wrap(~Epi_target, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "grey20", mid = "white", high = "firebrick",
                       limits = c(-1, 1), oob = scales::squish) +
  labs(x = "Log incidence, log(count + 1)", y = "Weekly growth in log incidence",
       fill = "Interaction\n(log scale)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "grey85", colour = NA),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
```
